sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: charityevals adjustments on top of ACE's model.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model, not ACE's. Ambitious Impact's suffering-adjusted days (SADs) count each species' pain as a share of a person's, using its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' estimates go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the one animal slider, under Your values.

rows.label: # hens affected per year
rows.explainer: ACE's input, source type: Charity's data.

rows.label: SADs averted per hen per year
rows.explainer: ACE's figure for a hen-year moved from a battery cage to cage-free, from Ambitious Impact's suffering-adjusted days. Our view uses the shared figure for the same change (Suffering-adjusted days per animal, under Data), so it counts the same in every model; the evaluator view keeps ACE's 17.486002148.

rows.label: # years commitments brought forward
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway" (5 by default), like every model that credits a won reform. ACE's own figure, 20.5 years (the midpoint of its bounds, 4 to 37), is kept as the evaluator's and used in the evaluator view.

rows.label: General annual discount rate
rows.explainer: Your discount rate (Timing, under Your values). ACE's sheet uses 4%.

rows.label: Years from winning the commitments until they take effect
rows.explainer: Ours, not ACE's. Kafessiz Türkiye's commitments were won in 2023 with deadlines a few years out (Turkish cage-free pledges mostly name 2025 to 2030), so the hens' lives change some years after the win. Our judgment: 4 years, 2 to 7. ACE counts the benefit from the year of the win; the evaluator view keeps that.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the commitments take effect
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: every model discounts the wait until a won reform takes effect at "Next year's good counts less by". ACE counts the hens from the year of the win, so the evaluator view uses 1.

rows.label: % responsibility for commitments
rows.explainer: ACE's input (source type: charity's data): ÇHKD takes all the credit for the commitments Kafessiz Türkiye won. Who caused a win is a judgment, not an observation, so filed as one; the range down to 50% is ours (other groups, the Open Wing Alliance's international campaigns among them, press some of the same companies). Used with "Credit by share of resources" off.

rows.label: ÇHKD's share of the resources all groups spent winning these commitments
rows.explainer: Ours. With "Credit by share of resources" on, a win is shared by what each group put into it, as GiveWell's models share an outcome by every funder's money. Kafessiz Türkiye is ÇHKD's own campaign, but international groups in the Open Wing Alliance also press the multinational companies among its targets. No group publishes what it spent per company; our judgment is 80%, 50% to 100%.

rows.label: Credit for the commitments
rows.explainer: ACE's responsibility (100%) by default; with "Credit by share of resources" on, ÇHKD's share of the resources behind the wins.

rows.label: % of companies that stick to their commitments
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared share of cage-free commitments companies keep (facts: sad_factors.commitment_fulfilment_cage_free, 92% of commitments due by 2024 fulfilled, Chicken Watch), as every model crediting a cage-free pledge does. ACE's own 63% (the midpoint of its bounds, 28% to 97%) is kept as the evaluator's and used in the evaluator view.

rows.label: Number of hens affected (discounted)
rows.explainer: Hens affected each year, over the years the commitments are brought forward, with later years counting less.

rows.explainer: Advocacy is mostly people, so staff pay is usually most of the budget. We haven't seen this charity's breakdown; the default is the same guess we use for other animal advocacy groups. Range is ours.

rows.explainer: Campaigners, researchers and negotiators could typically earn considerably more in comparable for-profit roles. Range is ours.

How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Your value, shared with every model built on an organisation's past average (Your values: "How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far"): ACE's estimate is ÇHKD's past year of campaign spending over the cage-free commitments it won, an average; the next dollar does less than the average dollar did, since an organisation pursues its best opportunities first. 50% by default (our judgment), from 18% to 100% (average = marginal). The evaluator view keeps 100%.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row above).

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give: chickens
Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: chickens
rows.explainer: The SADs for chickens with the hen weight built into the 2024 SADs ACE used (46% of a person's) taken out, which leaves days of a chicken's disabling pain. A chicken counts as 1 here by definition; how a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the chicken slider. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weight, so ACE's own result reproduces.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Days of disabling pain spared, all species, counted as a chicken's. The headline converts this into years of healthy life with the chicken slider and the healthy hours lost per day of disabling pain.
